The study focused on closed-canopy, undisturbed Scots pine stands and examined annual NDVI variation in 2016–2022 across eight forest natural regions in relation to stand age, stand volume, top height, and the Relative Spacing Index (RSI). Mean NDVI showed persistent regional differentiation across Poland and ranged from 0.64 to 0.84. The proportion of NDVI variability explained by stand characteristics varied markedly among years and forest natural regions, indicating strong spatial and temporal heterogeneity in NDVI–structure relationships. In general, structural predictors explained a larger share of NDVI variation in years with more favourable moisture conditions, whereas in drought years this structural signal was less apparent, partly coinciding with lower and more compressed NDVI distributions. An illustrative regional analysis further showed that the direction and magnitude of the partial effects of stand attributes changed among years, demonstrating that the structural meaning of NDVI was not constant through time. The results show that NDVI should not be interpreted as a spatially invariant proxy of stand structure across heterogeneous forest landscapes. Instead, its information content depends on both regional context and annual moisture conditions. By combining harmonized optical time series, LiDAR-derived stand descriptors and spatially varying modelling, this study provides a framework for more robust interpretation of canopy greenness in large-area forest monitoring.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: V-BUILD: A graph Transformer-based decision framework for selective updating of vector building data
abstract: Keeping vector building databases current requires deciding which database operations should be applied, rather than merely detecting binary geometric differences. Minor discrepancies caused by acquisition noise, representation style, or cartographic generalization may trigger unnecessary updates when using hand-tuned geometric thresholds. We present V-BUILD, a hybrid decision framework that assigns each matched building unit one of four operations: addition, deletion, replacement, or preservation. Deterministic rules handle existential decisions, while a geometry-aware graph Transformer learns the more ambiguous morphological decisions between replacement and preservation directly in the vector domain. The model encodes 1:1 to m:n matching relationships via Unified Correspondence Graphs and uses Adaptive Multi-stream Fusion to integrate node-, edge-, and graph-level geometric descriptors. Experiments on Amsterdam TOP10NL, Hamburg LoD1, and Mercer County OSM data, together with a difficult Amsterdam subset, show that V-BUILD performs well in within-domain evaluations on both authoritative and crowdsourced vector data, while leave-one-domain-out analysis indicates that direct cross-source transfer remains challenging under strong domain shift. On Amsterdam, V-BUILD achieves the best Replacement F1 of 89.44 %; on Mercer, it obtains the best Macro F1 of 88.51 %, outperforming the strongest GNN baseline by 4.22 percentage points; and on the difficult Amsterdam subset, it achieves a 4.51-percentage-point higher Replacement F1 than the strongest GNN baseline, with the associated reduction in paired sample-level errors confirmed by a two-sided exact McNemar test. These results indicate that V-BUILD reduces dependence on manually tuned geometric decision thresholds and provides a practical decision module for incremental vector building database updating.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Global cloud phase monitoring from FY-3G multi-angle polarimetric observations using the new MAPLE-CP framework with independent multi-site lidar validation
abstract: Global cloud-top phase monitoring is constrained by an observing gap: passive imagers provide broad coverage but limited vertical phase information, whereas active sensors provide stronger physical constraints only along narrow tracks. Here we develop MAPLE-CP, a Multi-Angle Polarimetric Latent-Enhancement framework for FY-3G PMAI cloud-top phase retrieval. MAPLE-CP links shortwave-infrared multi-angle polarimetric scattering information, DQ-1 ACDL cloud-top lidar labels, physics-guided feature screening, compact latent augmentation, and independent lidar validation. From approximately 140 PMAI variables, 50 physically interpretable predictors were selected and enhanced with six self-supervised latent descriptors. Using a 142,362-sample PMAI–ACDL cloud-top phase corpus, MAPLE-CP achieved internal accuracy, macro-F1, and AUC of 0.946, 0.897, and 0.991, respectively, on the original internal test split. Grouped split diagnostics clarified the evidence boundary of this internal benchmark, and independent validation using 6,433 ground-based lidar samples from 31 Chinese sites gave an agreement of 0.788 and macro-F1 of 0.780 within this external network. On an availability-limited shared-collocation subset with MODIS, Himawari-9, and ground-based lidar, MAPLE-CP showed higher agreement and macro-F1, suggesting complementary PMAI polarimetric phase information rather than a global product ranking. Overall, MAPLE-CP supports scalable cloud-top phase mapping and exposes residual mixed-phase uncertainty.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Deep spatial-spectral fusion of UAV RGB and hyperspectral imagery for potato plant disease detection
abstract: Accurate plant disease detection remains challenging when using single-modality data, which fails to capture comprehensive disease-related features. However, many existing studies rely on pixel-level classification or prior plant segmentation and lack explicit modeling of cross-modal interactions, limiting their ability to distinguish between healthy and diseased plants. This study presents a spatial–spectral fusion deep learning framework (S2-PDD) that fuses uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAV)-based RGB imagery and hyperspectral-derived feature representations for plant-level detection of potato diseases (blackleg and Potato virus Y (PVY)), employing early fusion (modalities combined at the input stage) and middle fusion (features integrated at intermediate stages within the model backbone) strategies. The multimodal fusion models were compared against single-modal models and an existing S2ADet model. Model performance, assessed through five-fold cross-validation, demonstrated that multimodal models integrating RGB and vegetation index features achieved the highest mAPs of 86.65 ± 1.71 (%; E-RV model) and 85.74 ± 1.96 (M-RV), respectively. These mAPs were higher than those of all single-modal models, including the RGB-only (83.21 ± 1.46) and hyperspectral-only models (PCA features: 79.71 ± 1.45; vegetation index features: 85.31 ± 2.36). They also exceeded mAPs of multimodal models combining RGB with PCA features (early fusion: 83.00 ± 2.81; middle fusion: 83.11 ± 2.46; S2ADet: 84.04 ± 2.73), regardless of the fusion strategy. The superior performance highlights that vegetation index features provide strong class separability compared to other hyperspectral representations. The proposed models achieved strong plant-level detection performance, with AP of 78.65 ± 4.14 (E-RV) and 77.40 ± 3.46 (M-RV) for blackleg disease, as well as 84.82 ± 3.59 (E-RV) and 83.28 ± 3.86 (M-RV) for PVY. These results demonstrate the potential of UAV-based multimodal sensing for disease monitoring in cropping systems. A potato plant disease detection dataset was constructed and made publicly available, containing paired RGB and hyperspectral image tiles with bounding box annotations. The code is available at https://github.com/Tim-Agro/S2-PDD.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: FSIF-PCNN: A physics-constrained neural network for full-spectrum solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence reconstruction
abstract: Full-spectrum solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF; 650–800 nm) provides a powerful means to characterize vegetation functional status. However, current retrieval methods still exhibit substantial uncertainties due to their reliance on fixed spectral-shape assumptions or strong priors for SIF and reflectance reconstruction, introducing inherent model-form biases when these assumptions mismatch observations. To address this limitation, we propose a physics-constrained neural network, FSIF-PCNN, for flexible and robust full-spectrum SIF reconstruction. FSIF-PCNN leverages a U-Net architecture to extract multi-scale spectral features, while enforcing physical plausibility through radiative-transfer consistency constraints and spectral smoothness regularization. The method was evaluated using simulated test datasets and independent tower-based measurements through comparison with two existing methods (FSIF-iPCA and SIFFI). On the simulated test datasets, FSIF-PCNN achieved minimal systematic bias (ARE = -0.034 %) and superior spectral reconstruction accuracy (RMSE = 0.011 mW m−2 nm−1 sr-1; mean RRMSE = 3.87 %), outperforming FSIF-iPCA (mean RRMSE = 13.70 %) and SIFFI (mean RRMSE = 11.98 %). Tower-based validations confirmed exceptional agreement with SFM retrievals in the O2-A and O2-B bands (site-specific R2 > 0.95). Compared with FSIF-iPCA and SIFFI, FSIF-PCNN demonstrated stronger accuracy and robustness across all validation sites, achieving site-mean RRMSE values of 5.74 % (DM), 4.46 % (GC), and 9.62 % (XTS) in the O2-A band, and 14.64 % (DM), 6.85 % (GC), and 11.22 % (XTS) in the O2-B band. These results demonstrate that FSIF-PCNN provides a flexible and physically constrained framework for full-spectrum SIF reconstruction, achieving improved agreement with independent references at the validated red and far-red bands.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Joint learning of frequency-spatio-temporal dependencies and structural context for optical-SAR change detection
abstract: Multimodal change detection combines multi-source remote sensing data, such as optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images, to overcome the inherent limitations of single-mode imaging mechanisms, thereby enhancing the robustness and timeliness of change information updates. However, previous Optical-SAR change detection methods still face challenges, including inadequate modeling of both modality-invariant and modality-specific characteristics, difficulty in capturing cross-modal spatio-temporal dependencies, and underutilization of land cover structural context. To address these issues, we propose a novel Optical-SAR change detection framework, namely FSTS-Net. It combines semantic features from the frequency, spatial, and temporal domains with structural features to comprehensively capture change. First, we design a frequency-spatio-temporal feature encoder integrating wavelet convolution and graph optimization theory into a state-space model to decouple cross-modal features and model bi-temporal dependencies. Second, a multi-scale graph convolutional network is built to explicitly model the spatial correlations among surface objects, thereby enhancing the representation of structural features. Finally, an adaptive fusion strategy dynamically adjusts the contribution weights of semantic and structural features to adapt to changes in information, effectively enhancing genuine change signals while suppressing pseudo-change. Our method demonstrates superior generalization and robustness over existing multimodal change detection (MMCD) methods, achieving mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 67.81 % on BRIGHT, 64.84 % on Wuhan-Het, and 88.55 % on Delta-SN6 datasets. The proposed FSTS-Net provides a reliable solution for multimodal change analysis. The code will be made available at: https://github.com/liuxuanguang/FSTS-Net.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Viewing-geometry effects on UAV-based tree height retrieval using BRDF-derived vegetation indices
abstract: Tree height is a key descriptor of forest canopy structure, yet a single nadir view captures only part of the directional structural information contained in canopy reflectance. This study investigated whether viewing geometry provides directional information useful for UAV-based optical tree-height retrieval in a Larix principis-rupprechtii plantation. Multi-angular reflectance observations extracted from overlapping UAV multispectral images were used to fit the RossThick–LiSparseR (RTLSR) kernel-driven bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) model. The fitted model was then used to reconstruct directional reflectance at 27 prescribed viewing geometries along the solar principal plane, while UAV-LiDAR data provided grid-level reference tree heights. Nine vegetation indices were derived and evaluated using linear regression, random forest, and gradient boosting regressor under single- and multi-angle schemes. DVI, EVI, GDVI, TVI, and GOSAVI exhibited consistent angle-dependent sensitivity to tree height, with their strongest correlations and lowest retrieval errors generally occurring within the intermediate forward-viewing sector (30°–45°) in the BRDF-derived dataset. For example, the absolute correlation between GDVI and tree height increased from 0.429 at nadir to 0.507 at 40°. Among the tested index–scheme–model combinations, the lowest validation error was obtained using GDVI under the Forward + 0° scheme with random forest, reducing RMSE from 2.19 m at nadir to 1.79 m (RMSE% = 10.25 %). However, the relative performance of the tested angular schemes varied among models, indicating that angular configuration and retrieval algorithm jointly affected performance, while increasing the number of angular features alone did not consistently reduce retrieval error. Overall, the findings indicate that viewing geometry can provide useful directional information for within-site optical tree-height retrieval and that intermediate forward-viewing information may complement nadir observations.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A multi-task collaborative method for individual tree segmentation and multi-dimensional attribute extraction in mountainous areas using deep learning technologies
abstract: Accurate mapping and monitoring of forest structure and composition in complex mountainous regions remain challenging because of crown occlusion, crown adhesion, and pronounced topographic variation. Moreover, current monitoring methods often focus on single-attribute retrieval and lack an integrated framework for collaborative multidimensional attribute extraction. To address these challenges, this study proposes a multi-task collaborative method for individual tree segmentation and integrated multidimensional attribute extraction in mountainous forests using deep learning and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB imagery. A two-stage segmentation method combining a U-Net++ deep learning model with a marker-controlled watershed algorithm was developed, followed by a sequential transfer learning strategy to facilitate knowledge transfer among individual tree segmentation, tree height prediction, and forest type classification. The proposed method was evaluated over a 5 km × 5 km area within the Wanglang National Nature Reserve (WNNR) using manually delineated tree crowns and canopy height models (CHM) derived from UAV LiDAR data. The results showed that the two-stage segmentation method combined the semantic representation capability of deep learning with the geometric partitioning ability of the watershed algorithm, thereby reducing under-segmentation caused by crown occlusion and adhesion in mountainous forests. The omission rate decreased from 9.12 % to 4.67 %, while the F1-score increased from 0.9298 to 0.9537. Sequential transfer learning also improved individual-tree attribute prediction, with the RMSE of tree height prediction decreasing from 7.1504 m to 3.4825 m and the overall accuracy of forest type classification increasing from 81.68 % to 92.51 %. The proposed method enables integrated mapping of individual-tree location, crown width, tree height, and forest type in complex mountainous forests, providing detailed information for precision forest management and forest carbon assessment.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Improving hourly PM2.5 estimation from geostationary satellite TOA reflectance through physically constrained multi-task learning
abstract: Geostationary satellite-based PM2.5 mapping increasingly relies on data-driven models using top-of-atmosphere (TOA) reflectance. However, most existing approaches train a single estimator on temporally aggregated samples, implicitly assuming a stationary relationship between TOA radiative signals and near-surface PM2.5. This assumption overlooks the pronounced diurnal variability captured by geostationary satellites and limits the representation of hour-dependent aerosol–radiation interactions. To address this limitation, we developed a physically constrained multi-task learning framework, termed the Multi-Temporal Decoupled Attention Network (MTDAN), for hourly PM2.5 estimation from geostationary satellite TOA reflectance. The framework integrates three components: (1) a physically guided surface–atmosphere decoupling module that suppresses surface-background interference and enhances aerosol-sensitive information; (2) a multi-task attention architecture that jointly learns shared and hour-specific relationships between PM2.5 and explanatory variables; and (3) a temporal-constrained loss function that exploits diurnal continuity to improve the consistency of sequential predictions. Experiments over eastern China using year-long Himawari-8 observations and ground-based PM2.5 measurements demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed framework. MTDAN achieved an overall site-based validation R2 of 0.89 with an RMSE of 9.27 μg m⁻3, outperforming representative machine-learning and deep-learning models by reducing estimation errors by 21.7 %–27.8 %. The model successfully reproduced hourly pollution evolution, captured localized hotspots, and reconstructed season-dependent diurnal PM2.5 dynamics. Ablation analyses further confirmed the complementary contributions of physical decoupling, adaptive feature weighting, and temporal-consistency constraints. These results demonstrate that explicitly modeling hour-dependent aerosol–radiation relationships can substantially improve geostationary satellite-based PM2.5 estimation. The proposed framework provides an interpretable and robust solution for high-frequency air-quality monitoring and offers a general strategy for integrating physical constraints and temporal context into Earth observation applications.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A multi-scale spatial-conditioned spectral routing network for hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion
abstract: Hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion (HMIF) aims to reconstruct high spatial resolution hyperspectral images by jointly leveraging the complementary spectral information from hyperspectral imagery and the spatial details from high spatial resolution multispectral imagery. Existing deep learning-based methods typically improve fusion performance by enlarging the receptive field to capture richer spatial–spectral contextual information, which inevitably increase computational complexity and may introduce redundant spatial–spectral interactions. To address these issues, this study proposes a new multiscale Spatial-Conditioned Spectral Routing Network (SCSRNet). Specifically, a Dynamic Fusion Gate (DFG) module is first developed to adaptively regulate the contributions of hyperspectral and multispectral features based on local spatial characteristics. Subsequently, a Large-Kernel Spatial–Spectral Residual Block (LK-SSRB) is designed, in which a Multi-Scale Spatial Perception Module (MSPM) captures spatial contextual information with large receptive fields, while a Spatial-Conditioned Spectral Routing Module (SCSRM) is innovatively designed to dynamically establish spectral dependencies guided by spatial priors. Additionally, a Residual Scaling Connection (RSC) is introduced to improve optimization stability and feature propagation efficiency. Extensive experiments conducted on three public datasets (i.e. Pavia Center, Chikusei, and MDAS) and a self-collected UAV-based Daxing dataset have demonstrated that the proposed method consistently outperforms seven state-of-the-art approaches in both quantitative metrics and visual quality. The performance gains of the proposed SCSRNet observed on the MDAS dataset achieves improvements of 6.0%, 9.8%, 0.7%, 9.7%, and 7.2% over the second-best comparative method. Furthermore, SCSRNet achieves superior reconstruction performance with relatively low computational complexity, underscoring its effectiveness and practicality for HMIF.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Tropoformer-S: iTransformer-based spatiotemporal reconstruction of three-dimensional tropospheric delay fields integrating ERA5 reanalysis and GNSS observations
abstract: Spatially continuous three-dimensional tropospheric delay fields are essential for Earth observation and atmospheric sensing. The ERA5 reanalysis offers continuous coverage but is delayed by several days, whereas Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations are accurate and near-real-time but pointwise. This study develops Tropoformer-S, an iTransformer-based framework that reconstructs the regional delay field by integrating the two sources. The framework forecasts the ERA5-derived level-wise Zenith Tropospheric Delay (ZTD) at 15 pressure levels from 1000 to 550 hPa for 1 to 120 h, where the variate-token attention explicitly models the spatial correlation among grid points. The forecast field is converted into station ZTD through a physically guided retrieval chain and refined by GNSS-informed corrections along two complementary paths, harmonic self-correction for stations with local GNSS records and spatial reconstruction of the bias field for stations without. Over mainland China, the forecasts attain a level-mean RMSE of 2.84 cm against the ERA5-derived ZTD and outperform five alternative deep-learning architectures. The overall RMSE is 3.20 cm in 2022 and 3.23 cm in 2023 against GNSS, on average 18.64 % and 33.10 % below GPT3 and HGPT2, and the radiosonde evaluation shows a near-zero bias. The harmonic correction path lowers the RMSE to 2.79 and 2.98 cm and reduces the network bias to near zero, while the spatial correction path reaches 2.10 to 2.66 cm at withheld stations under nine network densities and largely removes the lead dependence. The framework thus fills the ERA5 latency gap with continuous tropospheric delay information for geodetic and atmospheric applications.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Virtual geographical scene modeling towards geospatial digital twins: A case study of urban highway tunnel scenarios
abstract: As a virtual component of the geospatial digital twin (GDT), the virtual geographic environment (VGE) has significant advantages in enhancing human geographic cognition and analyzing and solving practical engineering problems. However, existing virtual geographic scene modeling methods still have significant gaps compared to GDT, making it difficult to balance the ability to represent dynamic objects as required by GDT while preserving the geographic characteristics of VGE, such as spatiotemporal reference and multiscale representation. Against this backdrop, this paper takes highway tunnel scenes as an example. It proposes a modeling framework that leverages the synergy between perception data and scene knowledge to construct a virtual geographic scene for GDT. First, we constructed a multi-domain integrated knowledge graph of highway tunnel scenes to enhance the standardization and completeness of the modeling process. Second, we established a dynamic object detection network based on an improved YOLOv8 model, endowing the virtual geographic scene with the capability to represent dynamic objects. Third, we proposed a tunnel scene twin modeling method that integrates a knowledge graph with a perception network, enabling effective fusion of the static base and dynamic objects. Finally, we selected a tunnel in China as the study area, developed a prototype system, and conducted experimental analyses. The results demonstrate that the proposed method successfully constructs a GDT-oriented virtual geographic scene for highway tunnels. For the city-level model, over 93.6 % of points have an error of less than 0.1 m; for the component-level model, over 95.4 % of points have an error of less than 0.01 m; the model’s semantic accuracy reaches 95 %; the average modeling time for dynamic targets is 11.8 ms; and the average rendering efficiency of the virtual scene is 133.2 FPS. Furthermore, compared to existing scene modeling methods, the constructed scene integrates advantages such as geospatial and temporal references, multiscale representation, and dynamic object representation. Research results provide an example reference for intelligent management of urban traffic, and provide new ideas for virtual geographical scene modeling.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: GICL-Net: A graph-interactive collaborative learning network for joint classification of HSI and LiDAR
abstract: Hyperspectral and LiDAR images, as a class of multi-source remote sensing data, have their own advantageous features. HSI contains rich spectral information, compared to LiDAR, which is more capable of reflecting the height information of the target area. However, determining the intrinsic correlation characteristics between HSI channels and fully exploiting the complementary characteristics of HSI and LiDAR to improve classification accuracy remains a challenging issue. In this paper, we propose a graph-interactive collaborative learning network (GICL-Net) for joint classification of HSI and LiDAR, which consists of a multi-scale spectral-spatial graph feature extractor (MSGE) and a cross-modality adjacency matrix fusion (CAMF) module. Specifically, MSGE is divided into two branches. One branch starts from the spectral dimension, defining each channel of HSI as a node to construct a graph network and mine potential correlations at the channel level, thereby capturing the intrinsic spectral correlation features of the target region. The other branch focuses on the height information of the target area, constructing a graph network at the geometric spatial level to extract representative height features. The CAMF module leverages the fused adjacency matrix to establish a cross-modal graph interaction mechanism, enabling the spectral features and the spatial features to achieve deep synergy through iterative updates in graph convolution. This generates cross-modal fusion features with fine spectral discrimination capability and spatial dimensional structural integrity. This method has been validated for effectiveness across multiple HSI and LiDAR datasets. In particular, on the Houston2013 dataset, the overall accuracy (OA) reached 98.91%, with a Kappa coefficient of 0.9882. Furthermore, compared with the baseline network (i.e., the conventional two-branch graph network, the overall accuracy improved by 6.58%. Our code is available at the link: https://github.com/Xidian-AIGroup190726/GICLNet.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Mapping selective logging with Sentinel-1 image time series and a novel transformer-based model
abstract: Selective logging (SL) is a major driver of forest degradation, yet its small and short-lived canopy openings remain difficult to detect in persistently cloudy tropical regions. Optical approaches miss many events, while synthetic aperture radar (SAR) time series are challenging to model with architectures that either fuse multivariate features too early or smooth over transient signals. We present InterFormer, a Transformer-based architecture that jointly models feature interactions and temporal dynamics via a feature block with Multi-head Intercross Self Attention (MISA) and a temporal block with Multi-head Self Dissimilar Attention (MSDA). Texture features were further utilized as complementary input. Since precise SL labels are unavailable, the model was trained and internally tested using a weak-label benchmark, in which pixel labels were extracted within the official published Real-Time Deforestation Detection System (DETER) polygons. To complement this internal weak-label benchmark, we designed two independent practical experiments to evaluate the model performance in low-intensity Annual Production Units (UPAs) based on field-inventory data and at the municipality scale (> 30,000 km2) in the Brazilian Amazon. In the independent UPA validation, InterFormer localized 92.65% of tree-falling gaps in UPA areas and outperformed standard Transformer variants and Planet-based alerts from the Brazilian Forest Service by approximately 20% at the tree level. At the municipality level, our predicted alert polygons achieved the highest Detection Rate against DETER across multiple reference-overlap thresholds in both Paragominas and Feliz Natal, while also producing fewer unmatched alerts than RAdar for Detecting Deforestation (RADD) and Tropical Moist Forest dataset (TMF). However, substantial over-expansion of predicted alert regions remained. These results suggest that InterFormer provides a useful framework for representing weak and short-lived SL signals in Sentinel-1 time series, and that openly available SAR data have the potential to support large-scale SL monitoring under weak supervision. Nevertheless, the current municipality-scale workflow still relies on optical-derived masking as a supporting step, and the development of a fully SAR-only large-area monitoring framework remains an important direction for future work.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: DecAttNet: A decoder-centric multi-task attention network for rapid, large-scale land use change detection and 2 M resolution products generation
abstract: To address the issues of insufficient resolution and a lack of fine-grained categories in traditional land use and land cover (LULC) products, this study integrates lightweight deep learning, a decoder-centric multi-task learning architecture, and a significant change attention mechanism to propose a deep learning framework (Decoder-Centric Attention Network, DecAttNet) for large-scale, high-precision land use change mapping. By mitigating cross‑task feature conflicts within the multitask‑learning framework via its significant‑change attention module, DecAttNet can adaptively focus on key change areas while sharing features and improving computational efficiency. Additionally, this study utilized DecAttNet to generate a 2023 land‑use product for North China (ten provinces, municipalities and autonomous regions) (LULC_NorthChina_2023) comprising 28 fine‑grained land‑cover classes based on 2‑meter high‑resolution imagery. The results of this study demonstrate that (1) DecAttNet significantly outperforms other deep learning models in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency, with an average overall accuracy of 90.28 %, which is higher than the figures achieved by the FCNN model (83.12 %), the ChangeMask model (87.73 %), the BGSNet model (86.63 %), and the TripleS model (88.24 %), while improving computational efficiency by approximately 44 % compared to the FCNN model. (2) Based on an independent field validation dataset, the DecAttNet model achieved high extraction precision (precision = 94.86 %) for changed land cover features. (3) The LULC_NorthChina_2023 dataset constructed in this study, which is based on the DecAttNet model, combines high precision (precision = 91.85 %) with high spatial detail. (4) The DecAttNet model demonstrates significant temporal generalization capabilities, achieving average classification accuracies of 89.23 % and 88.78 % in selected sample test regions in 2024 and 2025, respectively, with interannual variability of less than 1.5 %, and exhibits high stability across different geographic re. The DecAttNet framework provides an efficient and accurate solution for large-scale, high-resolution land use dynamic monitoring, and the resulting dataset serves as a valuable benchmark for fine-scale environmental research.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A directional feature excavation transformer for oriented detection of small-scale ships in dense SAR imagery
abstract: The precise oriented detection of dense and small-scale ships within Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery constitutes a significant challenge for automated maritime surveillance systems because of intense clutter, minimal target sizes, and arbitrary rotations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a coordinated multi-stage feature refinement framework, termed DiFE-TransOBB, tailored for dense SAR ship detection. Rather than relying on isolated module enhancements, the proposed architecture establishes a progressive interaction mechanism across structural, spatial, and frequency domains. Specifically, the Directional Feature Excavator (DiFE) module can extract geometry-aware structural priors to suppress isotropic clutter interference, the High-Resolution Spatial Fidelity Preservation Branch (HSFPB) preserves fine-grained localization details of tiny ships, and the Dual-Domain Interaction Fusion (DualFusion) performs conditional frequency-domain refinement guided by these spatial-structural cues to disentangle ship contours from unstructured high-frequency sea clutter. Evaluated on the newly constructed DenseSARShip-v1 benchmark and further validated on public datasets, DiFE-TransOBB achieved the highest detection performance among the evaluated methods while maintaining a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and cross-dataset generalization capability of the proposed framework for oriented ship detection in dense and cluttered SAR scenes.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Tracking diurnal aerosol dynamics and smoke transport over East Asia using multi-geostationary satellite fusion (GK-2B, Himawari-9, FY-4B)
abstract: Continuous, high-frequency observations of aerosol optical depth (AOD) are crucial for understanding aerosol dynamics and regional air quality. However, individual geostationary (GEO) AOD products suffer from distinct spatiotemporal gaps and uncertainties driven by cloud screening, surface-reflectance assumptions, and strict algorithmic quality controls. To address these limitations, we propose a deep-learning fusion framework synergizing the spectral, temporal, and geometric complementarities of three GEO satellites (GK-2B, Himawari-9, and FY-4B) over East Asia. Central to our framework is a TabNet-based dynamic feature selection mechanism that adaptively weights heterogeneous multi-sensor inputs to suppress local retrieval errors. To improve spatial generalization, we implement a two-stage transfer learning strategy: pre-training with spatially extensive MODIS data to establish large-scale spatial priors, followed by fine-tuning with ground-based AERONET observations. Compared to single-satellite baselines, the fused AOD product from May 2024 to April 2025 improves accuracy and spatiotemporal coverage. Specifically, it yields an overall cross-validation correlation coefficient (R) of 0.94, reduces root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 47 %, and increases valid hourly matchups by 33.5 %. Independent-site validation shows consistent generalizability (R = 0.88). Furthermore, evaluations of extreme events, including severe biomass-burning and dust transport episodes, demonstrate that the fused AOD product can reconstruct hourly plume gradients during rapid transport. By improving the temporal characterization of complex aerosol environments, this deep learning-driven fusion approach provides a useful foundational dataset for future regional air-quality analyses and chemical transport model assimilation.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Automated conversion of unstructured mesh models to structured parametric CAD models for architectural applications
abstract: Parametric models are foundational to Building Information Modeling (BIM) and digital construction, enabling efficient design, analysis, and lifecycle management. However, most 3D building models reconstructed from real-world data sources — such as 3D scanning, photogrammetry, or format conversion — are represented as unstructured mesh models. Although these meshes accurately capture geometric shape, they typically lack the parametric constraints, design intent, and procedural history inherent to native BIM objects. This semantic deficiency severely limits their direct applicability in workflows that require model editing, parametric adjustment, or semantic interpretation. To address this challenge, this paper presents an automated framework for semantic lifting of unstructured architectural mesh models into structured, procedural parametric CAD models. The proposed pipeline first analyzes the geometric and topological characteristics of the input mesh and employs a deep learning-based module to predict a plausible sequence of CAD modeling operations. Subsequently, a 2D parametric profile abstraction and parameterization module processes the geometric regions involved in the predicted operations, transforming them into constrained and editable 2D parametric profiles composed of basic geometric primitives, such as lines, arcs, and circles. Finally, a parameterization-driven reconstruction module executes the recovered operation sequence and parametric planar profiles within a CAD environment to procedurally regenerate a structured solid model with full parametric editability. Extensive experiments on diverse architectural datasets demonstrate the robustness of the proposed approach, showing that it can generate parametric CAD models that closely match the original mesh geometry while supporting reliable parameter-driven editing. This research provides an effective pathway for the semantic lifting of mesh-based building models, enabling their reuse in BIM reconstruction, digital twins, and architectural analysis applications.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Kinematic pattern interpretation of railway-corridor deformation from InSAR time series with transfer learning-based TCN
abstract: Railway-corridor deformation monitoring requires timely identification of localized displacement anomalies and characterization of their temporal evolution. Time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides spatially dense and high-precision displacement observations from repeated SAR acquisitions, but InSAR-based railway studies have largely remained rate-centered, leaving the kinematic information embedded in displacement time series insufficiently exploited. This study develops a kinematic interpretation framework that integrates InSAR displacement time series, transfer learning-based Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) classification, and multi-source environmental data to characterize railway-corridor deformation in terms of its occurrence, temporal evolution, and environmental context. Sentinel-1 images acquired from January 2022 to December 2024 were processed to retrieve LOS displacement rates and displacement time series along the Kunming–Yuxi section of the China–Laos Railway. To reduce dependence on labeled InSAR samples, a transfer learning strategy was adopted, in which the TCN was pre-trained using simulated displacement sequences and fine-tuned with labeled InSAR observations to classify six kinematic patterns: stable, linear, step, piecewise linear, power-law, and undefined. The corridor is generally stable, with a mean displacement rate of −0.26 mm/year and stable points accounting for 77.96% of observations. Linear and step patterns account for 12.66% and 7.87%, respectively. Strong subsidence zones, where the localized displacement rate reaches −28.43 mm/year, are dominated by linear deformation. Pattern-based interpretation further shows that non-stable deformation is associated with Quaternary unconsolidated sediments, paddy soils, fine-grained soil textures, and urban expansion areas. These results indicate that InSAR-derived kinematic patterns provide an effective interpretive layer for linking railway-corridor displacement, temporal evolution, and environmental context.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Multi-angular assessment of early-season defoliation: Evaluating the sensitivity of vegetation indices to NPV visibility in temperate broadleaved forests
abstract: Early-season forest decline in temperate broadleaved stands often lacks detectable biochemical stress signals, manifesting primarily through reduced foliage density and increased visibility of non-photosynthetic vegetation (NPV). This study investigated the spectral separability of green leaves and NPV components under varying levels of canopy defoliation. Using a crane platform, we collected in situ leaf- and canopy-level spectrometer measurements alongside co-aligned photography to quantify the visible fraction of NPV. We analyzed the multi-angular reflectance characteristics and evaluated 35 vegetation indices (VIs) —including green biomass metrics and specialized NPV indices —using Random Forest to identify optimal spectral and geometric configurations. Sunlit young foliage exhibited high forward scatter, creating a nadir reflectance minimum. At canopy level, a nadir minimum was driven by the gap distribution resulting from sustainable forest management practices. Consequently, the optimal viewing angle for top-ranking VIs (e.g., SNCBAO, Ctr2, mNDVI705) was near the hotspot geometry, minimizing shadowing and forest floor interference. While the total visible fraction of NPV remained mostly insensitive to viewing angles, its shaded proportion varied. VIs targeting green vegetation via red-edge and NIR domains consistently outperformed dedicated NPV indices based on SWIR cellulose and lignin absorption. This is attributed to low upper-canopy SWIR transmittance, which obscured the signals of the largely shaded NPV fraction. Top-performing VIs achieved R2 = 0.92 for NPV visibility prediction, improving by 21 % over the best SWIR indices and 11 % over the nadir view. To accurately detect initial defoliation and overcome forest floor interference, adopting off-nadir viewing geometries is advantageous for capturing the optimal signal.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Remote-sensing-assisted and in situ-constrained reconstruction of 4-hourly chlorophyll-a dynamics in inland lakes using vision Mamba and temporal attention
abstract: Chlorophyll a (Chl-a) is widely used to indicate eutrophication and bloom risk in inland waters, but daily Sentinel-3 observations alone cannot resolve transient sub-daily variability represented in partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a records. This study therefore develops VGTA (Vision Mamba–GKOA–TCN-Attention), a staged remote-sensing-assisted and in situ-constrained framework that integrates daily Sentinel-3 OLCI-derived priors with partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences and binary observation masks. A 20-dimensional OLCI-derived feature space provides spectral–spatial priors for Chl-a estimation and bloom-risk state identification. GKOA optimizes TCN-Attention to reconstruct masked values within partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences. Vision Mamba outperformed CNN– and Transformer-based models in Chl-a estimation, achieving 94.8% accuracy, a Macro-F1 score of 0.909, and a Bloom-F1 score of 0.870. Ablation experiments confirmed the contributions of bidirectional contextual modeling, positional embedding, selective state-space modeling, and gating. Under Missing Completely at Random, block-missing, and real missing scenarios, GTA improved reconstruction performance by 12.71–55.54% relative to the best baseline models. Uncertainty increased once continuous gaps reached seven days, defining a practical boundary of data-driven reconstruction. Chl-a fluctuations and bloom-risk transitions can unfold within a day, and daily satellite snapshots may blur their timing or miss short events. Reconstruction of masked time steps within partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences can support earlier identification of bloom-risk transitions, more timely field sampling and management responses, and temporally finer monitoring of inland waters.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Bridging cloud-induced gaps in MODIS leaf area index products using high-frequency geostationary satellite observations
abstract: Leaf Area Index (LAI) is a fundamental variable for characterizing vegetation canopy structure and ecosystem functioning. However, persistent cloud contamination substantially constrains the spatiotemporal continuity of LAI products derived from polar-orbiting satellite observations. In contrast, geostationary satellites provide dense temporal sampling, offering a valuable observational basis for filling data gaps in polar-orbiting satellite products. To bridge this observational gap, this study develops an observation-complementary framework that integrates high-frequency Himawari-8 Advanced Himawari Imager (AHI) observations with MODIS LAI products to achieve LAI reconstruction in cloud-prone regions. Within this framework, AHI observations are first used to retrieve LAI at a spatial resolution of 2 km using a Random Forest model trained with a high-quality MODIS-based benchmark dataset, and are then downscaled to 500 m using MODIS-derived spatial texture information. The reconstructed AHI LAI is subsequently integrated into low-quality or missing MODIS pixels to generate a fused AHI-MODIS LAI dataset over China. Validation against in-situ measurements and cross-comparison results show that the fused product maintains reasonable numerical consistency and stable temporal trajectories. Data availability increases from 70.70% to 90.90% under the 4-day compositing cycle. These results indicate that geostationary-polar-orbiting observation complementarity provides a practical pathway for improving the continuity and usability of optical LAI products in persistently cloudy regions, while remaining subject to the constraints of optical observations and cross-scale reconstruction assumptions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Fine-scale annual mapping and dynamic monitoring of shrub encroachment in alpine grasslands by integrating Sentinel-2 phenological features with Sentinel-1 structural information
abstract: Shrub encroachment can alter forage resources, soil–water processes, and landscape configuration in alpine grasslands, yet annual mapping remains challenging because shrub and herbaceous canopies converge spectrally and many apparent changes occur in diffuse ecotones. We developed a 10-m annual mapping framework integrating Sentinel-2 phenology, Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) time-series information, and topographic covariates to distinguish shrubland from grassland in Maqu County on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau from 2018 to 2024. A learned SAR-derived shrubland-grassland discrimination score (SGDS) was constructed from annual Sentinel-1 descriptors using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-regularized logistic regression to improve shrubland-grassland discrimination. In the 2024 benchmark experiment, the selected random forest (RF) configuration reduced classification error by approximately 17% relative to optical-only RF. SGDS outperformed the tested conventional SAR indices and the full SAR-statistics feature set, and adding SGDS increased RF accuracy from 91.26% to 92.47%. When the selected workflow was applied independently to each mapping year, annual overall accuracies ranged from 91.6% to 95.8%, based on the same 500 temporally screened reference locations spatially separated from the model-development samples. Nominal mapped shrubland area increased from 392.3 km2 in 2018 to 648.2 km2 in 2022 before declining to 560.4 km2 in 2024. Confidence and boundary-sensitivity analyses showed that the pronounced 2020–2021 increase was largely associated with low-confidence ecotonal pixels and decreased from + 96.91 to + 6.09 km2 as the mapped-class confidence threshold increased from 0.60 to 0.80, whereas the 2022–2024 decline remained negative under all tested confidence and boundary screens. Mapped shrubland area showed an apparent positive association with annual mean temperature, but this relationship was not robust after detrending and should be considered preliminary given the seven-year record. Overall, integrating learned SAR structural information with optical phenology improved annual shrubland-grassland mapping and provided a more reliable basis for interpreting mapped dynamics, with potential for locally calibrated application in comparable alpine regions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Robust hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits across species and spatial scales using GA-ELM
abstract: Plant functional traits provide critical indicators of ecosystem functioning, biodiversity maintenance, and plant adaptive strategies under environmental change. However, hyperspectral retrieval of mangrove functional traits remains challenging because trait-related spectral signals are strongly influenced by species composition, canopy structural heterogeneity, and intertidal background effects, leading to unstable trait-spectrum relationships across species and scales. To address these limitations, this study developed a genetic algorithm-optimized extreme learning machine (GA-ELM) framework for robust retrieval of mangrove functional traits under heterogeneous mangrove spectral conditions. Three key traits, including chlorophyll content (Cab), equivalent water thickness (EWT), and leaf mass per area (LMA), were retrieved for four dominant mangrove species using leaf-level hyperspectral measurements and canopy-scale GF-5 imagery. GA-ELM generally outperformed PLSR, RF, and conventional ELM in species-specific comparisons. Leave-one-species-out validation yielded R2 ranges of 0.61–0.75 for Cab, 0.60–0.72 for EWT, and 0.66–0.76 for LMA, indicating moderate predictive capability for previously unseen species, with performance varying among species and traits. At the canopy scale, GA-ELM achieved stable estimation accuracy for Cab, EWT, and LMA based on GF-5 imagery (R2 > 0.75), demonstrating that the framework can be independently calibrated for canopy-scale retrieval. Independent cross-regional validation yielded R2 values of 0.60, 0.49, and 0.44 for Cab, EWT, and LMA, respectively, indicating moderate but reduced cross-regional transferability. Spectral sensitivity and band-selection analyses revealed species- and trait-dependent patterns that provided context for interpreting variation in predictive performance. These results remain conditional on one GF-5 acquisition per site and 30 m mixed-pixel conditions, and broader tidal-stage and cross-sensor validation is still required. These findings demonstrate the potential of GA-ELM for hyperspectral retrieval and spatial mapping of mangrove functional traits.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Prior-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network (PISA-Net) for multi-parameter water quality retrieval in Poyang Lake using Sentinel-2 imagery
abstract: Accurate retrieval of water-quality parameters from remote-sensing imagery is essential for monitoring large inland lakes, yet pronounced spatial heterogeneity and limited transferability across varying environmental conditions remain major challenges. This study proposes a Prior-Informed Spatially Adaptive Network (PISA-Net) for multi-parameter water-quality retrieval from Sentinel-2 imagery in Poyang Lake. PISA-Net integrates a CNN branch for nonlinear spectral–spatial feature learning with a knowledge-guided branch based on empirical optical descriptors and coordinate-derived geographic priors. A geographic soft-assignment mechanism constructs the spatial prior vector, which conditions CNN features through Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), while a stop gradient consistency loss (SG-CL) promotes agreement between the two prediction pathways with controlled gradient propagation. Chl-a, TP, and CODMn were modeled independently and evaluated using 5-fold spatial-block cross-validation against six representative empirical, statistical, machine-learning, and deep-learning baselines. PISA-Net achieved R2 values of 0.6113, 0.5112, and 0.5054 for Chl-a, TP, and CODMn, respectively, consistently outperforming the strongest baseline, 2D-CNN, while reducing RMSE by approximately 29.6%, 21.4%, and 19.0%. An additional April 2018 cross-season experiment revealed substantial degradation under direct zero-shot transfer, whereas few-shot adaptation markedly reduced prediction errors, indicating useful cross-season adaptability after limited local calibration. Overall, PISA-Net provides a prior-informed spectral–spatial framework for water-quality retrieval under spatially heterogeneous conditions, while broader multi-season validation remains necessary to establish comprehensive seasonal generalizability.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A Metro-InSAR Risk Index for corridor-scale displacement risk diagnosis of urban rail infrastructure
abstract: Time-series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides dense displacement observations along urban rail corridors, yet converting point-based measurements into corridor-scale diagnostic information remains challenging. This study proposes the Metro-InSAR Risk Index (MIRI), a diagnostic index designed to convert multi-dimensional InSAR-derived displacement characteristics into displacement-related diagnostic levels for urban metro corridors. MIRI integrates displacement rate, cumulative displacement, local displacement heterogeneity, height-related variability, and temporal residual variability, thereby extending conventional velocity-based interpretation toward corridor-scale displacement-risk diagnosis. The framework was applied to the Kunming Metro Network using 198 descending Sentinel-1 images acquired from March 2018 to December 2024. The time-series InSAR results show that the network was generally stable, with line-of-sight (LOS) displacement rates mainly ranging from −6 to 3 mm/yr and 97.21% of coherent scatterers falling within the stable interval of −3 to 3 mm/yr. Localized displacement anomalies were mainly observed near line intersections, curved sections, construction-affected areas, and the Dianchi Lake shoreline. Based on MIRI, 78%, 17%, 4%, and 1% of valid points were classified as Levels D, C, B, and A, respectively, indicating a distribution dominated by lower diagnostic levels, with spatially confined Level-B and Level-A anomalies particularly along Lines 4 and 5 and in lakeside soft-ground areas. Multi-source contextual variables and XGBoost-SHAP analysis were further used to interpret the environmental, anthropogenic, operational, and displacement-gradient information associated with the MIRI-based diagnostic patterns. The results indicate that the spatial variation in MIRI is mainly associated with terrain-related conditions, corridor-scale displacement variation, metro operation, and urban development intensity. By deriving diagnostic levels directly from PSI-based displacement indicators, MIRI provides an InSAR-based screening tool for prioritizing displacement-related anomalies and supporting maintenance of urban rail transit systems.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Robust reinforcement learning multi-baseline phase unwrapping algorithm with JPEG-LS
abstract: Multi-baseline (MB) phase unwrapping (PU) breaks through the limitations of the phase continuity assumption, but existing MBPU algorithms cannot adapt well to noisy environments. A robust reinforcement learning integer programming multi-baseline PU algorithm with JPEG-LS (RL-MBPU) is proposed. First, the cutting plane–pure integer programming cut-selection process is formulated as a sequential reinforcement-learning problem. An efficacy-guided imitation strategy is used to initialize an MBPU-structure-aware single-cut policy, which is further optimized by an actor–critic method using Cut-PAR2-based trajectory returns to reduce the root-node proof cost. Finally, the initial ambiguity number solution is corrected using dynamic median edge detector based on JPEG-LS, and the PU is completed by using the prediction of the left, top, and top-left neighbors of the current pixel and combining it with the local gradient threshold determination. In both simulation and real data experiments, the RL-MBPU algorithm demonstrated stable PU performance, including computational efficiency and noise robustness for interferograms of different sizes. Compared with the minimum-cost flow and cutting plane–pure integer programming algorithms, the RL-MBPU algorithm reduces the root mean square error by approximately 61.2% and 14.5%, respectively, while improving efficiency by approximately 54.1% and 42.4%, respectively. This can further support high-precision interferometric synthetic aperture radar applications.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: 3D building wireframe reconstruction via edge point regression
abstract: Despite significant progress in point cloud–based 3D building reconstruction, the effectiveness of existing methods remains constrained by four major bottlenecks. These include the scarcity of high-quality annotated datasets, the pervasive incompleteness and noise in real-world point clouds, the substantial memory consumption incurred by the edge search space, and the lack of adequate geometric constraints in network designs, which often causes loss functions to fail in capturing the underlying 3D structural regularities. To address these challenges, we pre-train a self-supervised learning (SSL) framework on large-scale unlabeled point clouds to learn generic geometric representations, and subsequently fine-tune it using only a limited set of annotated roof samples for 3D wireframe reconstruction. The key contribution of this work is the proposal of a new SSL-based framework that utilizes geometry aware edge point identification to facilitate wireframe reconstruction and avoid missing corners, thereby mitigating issues related to dataset quality and computational complexity. Specifically, the framework first leverages a pretrained SSL-based feature extractor to generate robust point-wise representations under sparse and imperfect inputs. Building on these features, an edge point–guided regression module predicts the parametric attributes of roof wireframes. To effectively supervise the training of this regression module, we formulate a joint loss function that optimizes two complementary objectives: (1) minimizing the Euclidean distance between input points and their nearest line segments, and (2) reducing the distance between candidate edge points and their projections on the reconstructed model. Coupled with bipartite edge matching and an edge-aware non-maximum suppression strategy, the proposed method ensures geometric validity while reducing computational redundancy. Extensive experiments across three datasets of varying geometric complexity and scale (Dense, Building3D, and the large-scale Tallinn City dataset) demonstrate the framework’s effectiveness. The SSL-based pretrained model attains 97% corner precision and 91% edge precision for wireframe reconstruction on the Building3D dataset, surpassing conventional baselines and approaching the performance of fully supervised methods. Remarkably, even under limited supervision, specifically utilizing only 50% partially labeled data during fine-tuning, the model maintains strong accuracy with 86% corner precision and 67% edge precision, underscoring its advantages over current SSL-based approaches.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Towards fractional vegetation cover mapping in complex mountain environments through a knowledge-guided unmixing framework
abstract: Mountain vegetation dynamics serve as sensitive indicators of environmental change, making accurate fractional cover mapping of primary components crucial for understanding ecosystem responses. This task has been facilitated by multispectral satellite imagery, particularly Sentinel-2, which provides continuous observations. To translate these observations into fractional cover maps, existing studies typically apply fraction estimation models to synthetic spectra derived from field-measured signatures. However, limited field surveys in mountain terrain present a data bottleneck for synthetic spectra construction, while complex vegetation composition introduces spectral ambiguities that existing methods struggle to represent. Therefore, this study develops a knowledge-guided unmixing framework for annual mapping of the fractional cover of herbaceous vegetation, woody vegetation, and bare land in mountain environments using Sentinel-2 time series. Specifically, to overcome data bottleneck, we develop a knowledge-guided strategy that automatically builds adaptive physio-phenological feature spaces to extract representative signatures. To resolve spectral ambiguity, we incorporate nonlinear mixing mechanisms to synthesize spectra that better represent complex mixing relationships. The synthetic library was then used to train Unmix-Net, a spectral-temporal regression model for fraction estimation. The framework was applied to the central Qilian Mountains and southern Hengduan Mountains spanning broad climatic gradients, validated with high-resolution UAV data. It achieved MAEs of 12.38 %, 8.58 %, and 9.82 % for herbaceous, woody, and bare land, outperforming existing models by up to 7.80 %. When implemented across landscapes ranging from arid steppes and alpine meadows to tropical rainforests, the framework maintained comparable performance. The comparative experiments further confirmed that the proposed extraction strategy improved the balance of component estimates, while combining complementary mixing mechanisms reduced estimation errors. By integrating domain knowledge into data-driven learning, this framework supports spatially continuous fractional vegetation mapping in mountain environments.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Online ecological-prior-guided bitemporal Transformer for mapping potential Spartina alterniflora eradication areas in coastal tidal flats
abstract: Accurate monitoring of Spartina alterniflora eradication is essential for evaluating coastal wetland restoration and supporting invasive-species management. However, vegetation removal and natural surface variation can produce similar spectral changes in heterogeneous tidal flats, complicating image-based detection. To address this issue, we propose COAST (Coastal Online Adaptive Spatiotemporal Transformer), an online ecological-prior-guided bitemporal Transformer for mapping potential S. alterniflora eradication areas in the Jiangsu coastal tidal flats, China. The framework uses geographically weighted discriminant analysis (GWDA) posterior probabilities to represent spatially heterogeneous relationships between S. alterniflora pre-eradication spectral features and removal-related change. These probabilities provide soft supervision for a lightweight online prior encoder, whose output modulates bitemporal features through spatial prior gating. Training uses spatial-block out-of-fold GWDA predictions, and inference uses paired images with the prior generated from the pre-eradication image. Under a spatially separated evaluation design, COAST achieved the highest mean F1-score (95.00 %) and IoU (90.48 %) among the evaluated baselines across three random-seed runs. It also achieved a boundary F1-score of 81.25 %, a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 256.04 m, and a changed-area fraction mean absolute error of 0.82 percentage points. Ablation experiments supported the contribution of prior-guided learning relative to the BiT backbone. Evaluation on manually annotated cross-year patches yielded F1-scores of 88.27 % for 2020–2023 and 93.13 % for 2020–2025, supporting temporal transfer within the sampled coastal settings. Local errors included agricultural-background false positives and incomplete target recovery. COAST provides an image-based workflow for repeated regional screening of eradication-related change and the prioritisation of follow-up verification.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Tree crown mortality and defoliation assessment in temperate forests using aerial imagery and deep learning
abstract: Forest health is increasingly threatened by global warming and recurrent droughts. However, limited long-term data on tree health and mortality restricts our ability to detect trends and predict forest responses to climate stressors. Traditional methods for assessing tree defoliation are accurate but costly and labor-intensive, highlighting the need for scalable alternatives. This study aims to develop a more automated approach for monitoring tree defoliation and mortality in Germany and Switzerland using deep learning applied to freely available aerial imagery. We assessed crown vitality using three and four defoliation classes derived from field surveys. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was trained on 48,388 annotated tree crowns from aerial imagery, labeled with forest type and defoliation status. RGB and NDVI-GB inputs were tested using five-fold and spatial-block cross-validation to ensure robustness. The three-class model outperformed the four-class CNN object detection version. RGB and NDVI-GB bands produced similar results in the three-class setup, with F1-scores of 0.74 and 0.73, respectively. Defoliated trees were more challenging to detect (F1-conifer: 0.61, F1-broadleaf: 0.54). Dead trees were detected with high accuracy (F1-score: 0.97), while healthy trees also showed good performance (F1-conifer: 0.78, F1-broadleaf: 0.73). Repeated aerial imagery revealed a 17-fold increase in standing dead trees across a 977-ha protected forest between 2014 (1,062 trees) and 2022 (17,897 trees), with 90 % of the increase after 2018. This study demonstrates that RGB imagery alone is sufficient for operational, tree-level monitoring of both defoliation and mortality over time. As more countries acquire repeated aerial imagery, this study offers broad applicability and supports forest inventories and resilient management strategies.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Process-informed deep learning for interpretable forested wetland mapping under dense canopy
abstract: Canopy-obscured hydrologic signals and gradual wetland–upland transitions hinder the delineation of forested wetlands, particularly when heterogeneous Earth-observation evidence is fused as an unstructured feature stack. We developed a process-informed multi-stream convolutional neural network (CNN) for mapping forested wetlands on a 10-m modelling grid in the Changbai Mountains, China. The model used 85 covariates derived from Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, ALOS-2 PALSAR-2, and Copernicus DEM GLO-30. These covariates were assigned a priori to five predictor streams and processed by separate CNN branches before fusion. Relative to a capacity-matched single-stream baseline, the grouped architecture increased forested-wetland F1 by 3.42 percentage points across five validation folds, whereas the gain on the fixed held-out test set was smaller (+1.03 percentage points). For map production, the probability-averaged five-fold ensemble achieved an overall accuracy of 0.873, a macro-F1 of 0.882, and a forested-wetland F1 of 0.836 on the fixed held-out test set. To interpret correlated predictors, group-aggregated SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and k-nearest-neighbor conditional replacement were used to characterize global and conditional model reliance. Among correctly classified forested-wetland samples, global reliance was greatest for temporal features and phenology, whereas conditional replacement indicated the greatest residual model reliance for hydrology, followed by topography. Direct pixel counting yielded a map-derived forested-wetland area of 686.6 km2, concentrated mainly in peripheral plains and hills. This framework combines process-informed feature organization with dependence-aware interpretation to support interpretable regional mapping of canopy-obscured forested wetlands.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: PSGRNet: Multi-scale spectral–frequency representation learning with gated residual fusion for coastal wetland classification using UAV hyperspectral imagery
abstract: Coastal wetlands are characterized by diverse vegetation, high spectral similarity, fragmented spatial distributions, and dynamic environmental conditions, posing significant challenges for accurate hyperspectral image classification. Although UAV hyperspectral imagery provides fine-grained spatial and spectral observations that can help capture such complex and fragmented features, effectively leveraging this information to distinguish spectrally similar and spatially intermixed vegetation types remains an open problem. Therefore, we propose a Progressive Spectral Gated Residual Network (PSGRNet). Specifically, a spectral enhancement and multi-scale sequence modeling strategy is first introduced to strengthen discriminative spectral representations and capture multi-scale spectral dependencies. Building on these enhanced representations, a frequency-aware module further exploits global frequency-domain characteristics to aggregate informative spectral features adaptively. To effectively integrate both spectral and frequency-domain representations, a GRF strategy is developed to improve the robustness of the network in heterogeneous and fragmented coastal wetland scenes. We have collected three UAV-based hyperspectral datasets covering representative coastal wetland scenarios, including reed-dominated natural wetlands (NT-YK), highly fragmented landscapes with dynamic land-cover transitions (YC-YS), and human-influenced estuarine environments (LYG-LH). Experimental results on these three datasets demonstrate that PSGRNet outperforms 9 representative methods, achieving macro F1 scores of 89.25%, 81.99%, and 81.29%, respectively. These results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method for accurate coastal wetland classification and demonstrate the value of the released datasets. The datasets will be publicly available at https://github.com/HAPPYFST/Wetland-HSI-Data.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Hierarchical active learning for annotation-efficient 3D object detection in construction-scene LiDAR sensing
abstract: 3D object detection in construction-scene LiDAR sensing remains challenging because sparse returns, irregular layouts, heavy occlusion, and diverse machinery make object representation and localization difficult. Dense manual annotation in such scenes is also inefficient and costly, creating a strong need for annotation-efficient learning. Existing active-learning methods often struggle in this setting because they tend to favor uncertain but redundant samples while overlooking representative scene coverage. To address this problem, we propose Hierarchical Clustering-enhanced Active Learning (HCAL), an active-learning framework for LiDAR-based 3D object detection in construction and roadwork environments. HCAL improves sample selection under limited labeling budgets by identifying informative candidate keyframes, suppressing redundant uncertain samples, and preserving representative coverage through entropy filtering, gradient-space clustering, and density-consistency selection. To support field-relevant evaluation, we further establish ConVeh3D as a construction-scene LiDAR benchmark for annotation-efficient 3D detection and unknown-category-aware evaluation in a controlled category-withheld setting. Experiments on ConVeh3D, with KITTI as secondary supporting evidence, show that HCAL achieves the best average detection accuracy across most tested labeling budgets. The results indicate that HCAL provides an effective framework for improving sample efficiency in construction-scene LiDAR-based 3D object detection under limited labeling budgets. The dataset and code will be made available at https://github.com/zxk688/ConVeh3D.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: WeavingUnet: Enhancing dense road extraction by integrating horizontal and vertical features
abstract: Road extraction plays a crucial role in automatically identifying road networks from remote sensing images, which is essential for various applications. However, existing road extraction methods perform poorly when dealing with dense roads. Inspired by the act of ”weaving” in real life, this paper proposes a dense road extraction method named WeavingUnet, aimed at addressing the difficulties in effectively extracting dense roads using existing methods. This model explores a novel approach to road feature extraction by analyzing road features in various directions and simulating the geometric shapes of roads to more accurately perform dense road extraction. The model incorporates innovative components such as Snake Weaving Attention, Contextual Information Weaving Module, Global Information Extraction Module, and Multi-Scale Weaving Decoder, which collectively enhance the extraction of multi-level road information and optimize the road reconstruction process. The model is tested on the public datasets DeepGlobe and Massachusetts, achieving F1 scores of 82.73% and 72.52%, and IoUs of 71.44% and 61.01%, respectively. Compared with the latest SOTA models, the F1 scores increase by 1.53% and 1.22%, and the IoUs improve by 1.76% and 1.87%. This study also conducts a comprehensive analysis of dense road extraction and compared it with SOTA models. In the densest areas, the false negative rates (FNs) in the test images are reduced by 4.93‰ and 1.47‰, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of WeavingUnet in handling dense roads. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/XianZhi-Ma/WeavingUnet.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: SAM-powered building footprint updating for various cities: Sparse labels meet historical data repurposing in urban monitoring
abstract: Accurate building footprint databases are fundamental for sustainable urbanization yet face persistent updating challenges due to the rapid pace of urban change. Traditional methods rely on bi-temporal image comparison for change detection, which requires a large number of new labels to retrain the model, which is costly. We propose a passive updating paradigm that eliminates the reliance on historical imagery and leverages a lightweight adaptive strategy applied to Segment Anything Model (SAM) to minimize labeling costs. Furthermore, we propose a Cross Modal Temporal Fusion (CMTF) module that combines features from historical building footprints with those from recent imagery, alleviating the burden of small-sample training. The training process utilizes a semi-supervised approach, enabling the model to learn from both labeled and unlabeled regions, with labeled regions comprising only 0.4% of the building samples. Besides, we propose the RIO dataset, a sub-meter bi-temporal building footprint update dataset for studying building changes in rapidly developing areas. In addition, this work is validated on a range of cities worldwide, including Christchurch (post-earthquake reconstruction) and Beijing-Shanghai (megacity expansion). This work advances urban building renewal by overcoming the reliance on paired historical imagery for change detection and the need for large amounts of up-to-date labels. This approach offers a scalable solution for monitoring SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), enabling less developed countries to use free and open product data to track urban expansion patterns with only a few labels.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: MT-RoadNet: A heterogeneous network with local–global joint enhancement for road surface and centerline extraction
abstract: Road network information has extensive applications, such as urban planning and navigation. However, current road extraction methods mostly rely on single model architectures and single-source remote sensing images, neglecting the potential benefits of collaborative extraction with heterogeneous networks and multi-source data fusion. Moreover, existing methods often suffer from road fragmentation and poorly connected road graphs due to occlusions. To address these challenges, we propose MT-RoadNet, a local–global joint enhancement framework for extracting road surfaces and centerlines, which incorporates multi-network collaborative optimization. Specifically, MT-RoadNet adopts a dual-branch structure, which not only facilitates the collaborative extraction of local details and global semantics but also achieves the coupling of geometry and topology through a cross-task dynamic interaction mechanism. Besides, we propose the Local–Global Feature Fusion module (LGFF), which dynamically integrates local details and global semantics through multi-level feature interaction. Furthermore, to reduce interference features with high inter-class separability and low intra-class variation, we innovatively design the Visual State Space Module (VSSM) and the Spatial-Channel Mutual Attention (SCMA). The VSSM weighs features dynamically using multi-directional cross-scanning and global receptive fields, emphasizing prominent area information while improving computational efficiency. SCMA effectively guides the model to focus on semantically relevant regions. Finally, MT-RoadNet adopts a dual-path decoder to produce road surfaces and centerlines.
