Extensive experiments on three road datasets demonstrate that MT-RoadNet significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of road completeness and recognition accuracy of topological structure. The code is available at https://github.com/508hz1207/MTNet.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: EL-Mamba: An edge-aware and locally-aggregated Mamba network for building height estimation using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery
abstract: Building height is critical for understanding urban morphology and promoting sustainable growth. Although numerous approaches using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and optical images have been proposed for estimating building height, two key challenges remain: 1) neglecting edge characteristics results in inaccurate building boundary delineation; and 2) failure to capture both global and local context reduces height estimation reliability. To address these limitations, a novel edge-aware and locally-aggregated Mamba model is proposed, namely EL-Mamba. In this model, an edge-aware module is designed to enhance building boundary representation through multi-scale Laplacian of Gaussian (LoG) filtering. Additionally, a local aggregation strategy is integrated into Mamba’s global scanning mechanism, which enables the network to effectively capture global and local context. Building height data from Wuhan and the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) region in China is selected to evaluate EL-Mamba’s performance. The results indicate that compared to the four existing methods, EL-Mamba achieves the lowest root mean square error (RMSE), with values of 4.963 and 5.358 on the Wuhan and YRD datasets, respectively. Furthermore, EL-Mamba exhibits high computational efficiency and reliable generalization capability, indicating its significant potential for application in large-scale areas. Our implementation is available at: https://github.com/ohXu/EL_Mamba.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: RPDNet: Street-level road pavement damage detection with a real-time anchor-free network
abstract: Accurately and timely detecting road pavement damage helps monitor road deterioration extent, thereby guiding maintenance projects and ensuring traffic safety. Nevertheless, due to textural similarity and nested distribution between neighboring pavement damages, as well as the damages with the diversity sizes, irregular shapes, multiple categories, current methods have the limitation in the high-quality detection from road street-level images. To tackle these challenges, this paper develops a novel real-time anchor-free network with a one-stage processing architecture, named RPDNet, for precisely and accurately detecting pavement damages from streel-level road images. First, stacked with a layer-by-layer encoding structure boosted by a deformable fully-attentive module as the backbone extractor, the RPDNet can capture more fine-grained information and generate multiscale strong task-aware semantics, favoring significantly the discrimination noteworthy textural and geometric features. Then, by adopting a multi-level efficient aggregation neck, the RPDNet can promote informative spatial details and integrate the different-level damage encoding features, contributing to the light-weight and optimization of the whole architecture. Afterward, designed with a dual-large kernel module, embedded in a decoupled detection head with anchor-free guidance, the RPDNet can project the ranging dependency of salient and task-oriented pavement damage objects by adaptively aggregating information across large kernels in spatial-domain. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations confirmed that the RPDNet provided a promiseful solution for detecting pavement damages in industrial applications under complex street-level road conditions. Furthermore, comparative analysis with the latest anchor-based and anchor-free alternatives also proved the superiority and generalization of the RPDNet in pavement damage detection tasks. The assessment results displayed that the RPDNet obtained an average mAP@0.5, mAP@0.5:0.95, precision, and recall of 69.16%, 44.86%, 72.59%, and 60.41%, respectively, on two dataset. Additionally, we constructed a large-size multi-city road pavement damage image dataset to support urban road health monitoring.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: MISNet: Multi-task interaction Siamese network for 3D point cloud semantic change detection
abstract: 3D semantic change detection enables the detection and identification of both changes in urban objects and their semantic categories, providing fine-grained change information for downstream applications. Existing methods rely on single-branch architectures with predefined output labels, which is simple but suffers from complex output definitions and ineffective multi-task coupling, compounded by scarce annotated 3D realistic data. To overcome these challenges, firstly, two 3D realistic semantic change detection datasets are constructed and published, named HKSCD and UtrechtCD , which utilize oblique photogrammetry point clouds and LiDAR point clouds to describe 9 semantic categories and 2 change types in Hong Kong, China, and Utrecht, Netherlands, covering 15 square kilometers with 370 million points. Secondly, a Multi-task Interaction Siamese Network (MISNet) for 3D point cloud semantic change detection is proposed. It deeply couples semantic segmentation and change detection, enabling the simultaneous prediction of both tasks within a unified architecture. The proposed multi-dimensional change encoding module computes cross-temporal neighborhood relationships from multiple dimensions to extract accurate point cloud change features. Additionally, the change-guided semantic refinement module and the semantic-awareness change interaction module leverage change information to support semantic consistency and utilize semantic information to assist inter-class change detection to promote cross-task consistent modeling underpinned by the cross-learning strategy. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MISNet achieves mIoU of 84.15% (HKSCD), 85.15% (UtrechtCD), and 89.58% (Urb3DCD-V2), outperforming existing methods by + 2.21%, +1.43%, and + 1.46%, respectively. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/zhanwenxiao/UrbanSCD and https://github.com/zhanwenxiao/MISNet.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: SAM-assisted weakly supervised semantic segmentation framework for plastic greenhouses mapping using high resolution imagery
abstract: Plastic greenhouses (PGs) are important infrastructure for modern protected agriculture, and their accurate high-resolution mapping is essential for agricultural planning and environmental protection. However, most existing approaches rely on fully supervised semantic segmentation (FSSS), which requires dense pixel-level annotations and hinders large-scale deployment. Image-level weakly supervised semantic segmentation (WSSS) offers a more scalable alternative but suffers from poor-quality pseudo-labels in initial generation stage and unreliable supervision for final training. Specifically, during pseudo-labels generation, coarse class activation maps (CAMs) with overly concentrated high-response areas and insufficient multi-scale details, together with conventional CAMs-to-label conversion methods, struggle to recover accurate boundaries and preserve object completeness. Moreover, inevitable noise in the generated initial pseudo-labels may mislead model optimization and degrade generalization performance. To address these challenges, we propose a novel image-level WSSS framework termed SAM-assisted Semantic Segmentation (SASS) for large-scale PGs mapping from high-resolution images using only image-level labels. SASS integrates multi-level high-resolution CAMs (MHCAMs) with regional priors derived from the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to generate more complete and boundary-aware pseudo-labels. Besides, a noise suppression strategy with aid of region filtering is further developed to enhance label reliability for final segmentation model training. Finally, a localization-then-extraction strategy is adopted to efficiently map PGs distribution (2.4 m) in Shandong Province, China, achieving overall accuracy and F1 score exceeding 90%. Extensive experiments and comparisons demonstrate that SASS exhibits advantages in accuracy and efficiency and can provide a scalable and transferable solution for large-scale mapping applications.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: HSRRSFPD and MEGRDNet: empowering high-resolution farmland parcel mapping in complex terrains
abstract: Existing methods in farmland extraction tasks still face limitations due to significant scale differences among farmland parcels and insufficient boundary perception capabilities, which undoubtedly hinders the promotion and application of large-scale and detailed farmland parcel mapping. To address these technical challenges of fine-grained farmland extraction in complex terrain areas, this study constructed a high spatial resolution remote sensing farmland parcel dataset (HSRRSFPD) covering multiple geomorphic regions (plains, hills, and mountains). HSRRSFPD includes 8,441 image chips with sizes of 256 x 256 pixels, and its total coverage area exceeds 550.00 km2. Based on HSRRSFPD, a novel multi-scale edge Gaussian refinement dual-branch network (MEGRDNet) was proposed for refined farmland parcel mapping. MEGRDNet integrated a multi-scale spatial (MSS) branch to address the challenges posed by the diversity of spatial scales of ground objects. Additionally, an edge Gaussian refinement (EGR) branch was developed to enhance the continuity and integrity of farmland boundaries. Compared with existing state-of-the-art algorithms, MEGRDNet achieved maximum improvements of 20.03% in IOU and 10.45% in F1 score. It significantly enhanced the accurate representation of multi-scale farmland boundaries under different terrains. Furthermore, the synergistic effect of the MSS and EGR branches improved MEGRDNet’s IOU performance by 21.93% compared to the Baseline model. In practical applications, a main grain-producing region (Sichuan Province) in China was used for fine-grained farmland parcel mapping at a 1 m spatial resolution. The results were highly consistent with the local government statistical data (GSD). Compared with existing farmland products, MEGRDNet provided finer boundary information, higher spatial resolution, and more accurate spatial representation. The findings and methods of this study are of great significance for land resource optimization, crop monitoring, and food security assurance in complex terrain regions of China or globally.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: PMTB-VSRnet: A video super-resolution network with radiometric consistency guidance for Antarctic passive microwave brightness temperature
abstract: Monitoring Antarctic surface melt using satellite-based Earth observation relies heavily on passive microwave data for their all-weather capability; however, their coarse spatial resolution limits the detection of fine-scale melt features. To address this limitation, we propose PMTB-VSRnet, a video super-resolution network with radiometric consistency guidance for Antarctic passive microwave data. In PMTB-VSRnet, neighboring frames are first aligned using Pyramid, Cascading and Deformable (PCD) alignment, while low-frequency Normalized Cross-Correlation (NCC)-guided fusion enhances radiometric feature consistency and suppresses unreliable observations. The aligned features are then propagated bidirectionally to exploit temporal information and reconstruct fine-scale brightness temperature structures. Finally, a radiometric high-frequency constraint is introduced to enhance reconstruction accuracy. Extensive experiments on AMSR2 multi-channel data show that PMTB-VSRnet outperforms all compared methods, improving PSNR over the average performance of the competing methods by 1.57, 2.30, 2.47, and 2.81 dB for the 36.5H, 36.5V, 18.7H, and 18.7V channels, respectively, under a 4× super-resolution setting. Additional experiments across diverse Antarctic terrains, seasons, and continent-scale regions further demonstrate the robustness and scalability of the proposed framework. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/jingli1999/PMTB-VSRnet.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A data- and knowledge-driven cropland parcel recognition method based on segment anything model (SAM)
abstract: In modern agricultural practices, information on cropland parcels serves as an indispensable foundation of agricultural production management. However, manual annotation of remote sensing image datasets is time-consuming and labor-intensive. Traditional models tend to focus on pixel-level segmentation while neglecting the fine-grained boundary features of cropland parcels. To address these challenges, this study first utilizes the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to generate cropland parcel label samples based on multi-source remote sensing imagery and the Third National Land Survey (TNLS) data. Morphological processing and texture feature screening are employed to enhance the quality of pseudo-labels. Subsequently, we propose a multi-task intelligent cropland parcel extraction model, Squeeze-and-Excitation Multiple Task Decoder Network (SE-MTDNet). This model adds a Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) channel to RGB channels to extract hierarchical features. The atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) module and channel attention are introduced to aggregate multi-scale contextual information. In the decoder, multi-task joint training is adopted to prevent over-reliance on the single results. Experimental results demonstrate that SE-MTDNet significantly improves both the accuracy and boundary clarity of cropland parcel recognition. In Xi County, SE-MTDNet achieved an overall classification accuracy of 94.25%, an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 88.67%, and an F1-score of 92.76%. Furthermore, the model also outperformed other comparison models in transfer validation conducted in Lishu County. Ablation experiments further confirm that key modules and the NDVI feature contribute significantly to improved cropland parcel segmentation accuracy. Our method provides valuable insights into high-precision and automated cropland parcel recognition.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Global retrieval of stokes vector of water-leaving radiance via Unet-based framework
abstract: The polarization characteristics of water-leaving radiance (Lw) exhibit marked sensitivity to the micro-optical properties of oceanic particles, making multi-angle polarimetric observations a crucial approach for solving nonlinear, ill-posed, and underdetermined radiative transfer (RT) equations in ocean color remote sensing. However, most existing statistically optimized search-based atmospheric correction (AC) models neglect the multi-angle Stokes vector contribution of Lw in retrieving polarimetric aerosol properties. In this study, a polarization-based AC model for the multi-angle Stokes vector of Lw was developed using Fully Connected U-net (FUCN-AC) and global RT simulations database. And, the global spatial distribution patterns of inversion errors for the Lw Stokes vector, and the impact of instrument noise on the FUCN-AC with respect to observation geometry, were systematically investigated. The results showed that the global mean absolute percentage errors (MAPEs) for the Lw Stokes parameters (I, Q, and U), remote sensing reflectance (Rrs), aerosol optical thicknesses (AOTs), and degree of polarization (DOP) at 490 nm were 2.24 %, 5.86 %, 6.38 %, 2.2 %, 15.94 %, and 6.06 %, respectively. The maximum MAPE for each parameter in coastal waters were mainly concentrated along the coastlines of the Eurasian continent in the Northern Hemisphere and the coastal waters of Antarctica. Additionally, field-measured polarized radiances validated the FUCN-AC model with a MAPE of 39.84 % for DOP, which might be attributed to uncorrected instrumental polarization and aerosol model mismatches. Moreover, the FUCN-AC model demonstrated significantly larger MAPE for the Stokes parameter Q and AOT at 490 nm, exceeding those for Stokes parameter I by factors of approximately 4.12 and 4.95, respectively. Furthermore, instrument noise exerted the most pronounced impact on Stokes parameter I and Rrs, with the MAPEs increasing by factors of 2.54 (3.80) and 2.61 (3.90) under 3 % (5 %) noise levels, respectively. Overall, the FUCN-AC achieves the nonlinear decoupling between atmospheric and ocean polarization signals, and provides technical support for the large-scale, high-frequency dynamic monitoring of the multi-angle Stokes vector of Lw.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: WaterPLNet: A noise-robust weakly supervised network for water extraction from SAR imagery using point labels
abstract: Existing methods for water extraction from Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery rely on labor-intensive and costly pixel-level annotations, which demand expert knowledge of SAR backscatter characteristics, significantly hindering the large-scale application of water extraction models. Although Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS) can mitigate this label-dependence limitation, the label sparsity inherent in existing methods limits the accuracy of water extraction, exacerbated by speckle noise and insufficient regional spatial semantic information. To address these challenges, a noise-robust weakly supervised Network for high-precision Water extraction (WaterPLNet) from SAR imagery is proposed that leverages only Point Labels. First, a Noise-Robust Network (NRNet) with an asymmetric dual-branch structure is proposed, which enhances feature robustness and mitigates noise-induced accuracy degradation by introducing Gaussian perturbations. Second, a Prior-Guided Region Expansion (PGRE) module is designed to identify potential water regions and mitigate false negatives arising from insufficient spatial semantic information. Finally, a Low-Backscatter Ambiguity Reduction (LBAR) module is proposed to leverage point labels and low-scattering priors, thereby reducing confusion between water and similar low-backscatter land covers. Experiments conducted on three datasets of SAR images collected from the Gaofen-3 and Sentinel-1 satellites covering typical spatial resolutions (1 m, 3 m and 10 m) demonstrate that WaterPLNet reduces reliance on labeled data while achieving state-of-the-art performance compared to other WSSS approaches using point labels. Specifically, WaterPLNet achieves an overall accuracy of over 93% across all datasets, with an mIoU that outperforms other methods by an average of 5.48%. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/Kiwi-xd/WaterPLNet.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: A physical Scattering-Guided Prior-Enhanced Mamba model for high-fidelity SAR ship generation in complex backgrounds
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image synthesis remains challenging in Earth observation (EO) due to unique speckle noise and the high dynamic range of backscatter coefficients. Existing models typically rely on direct pixel-wise synthesis, ignoring physical scattering mechanisms. This causes textural distortions that hinder downstream geospatial interpretation. To address these bottlenecks, we propose a physically-guided, coarse-to-fine generation framework, Scattering-Guided Prior-Enhanced Mamba (SGPMamba). Specifically, a Scattering-Guided Prior (SGP) model is introduced to transform multiplicative speckle into an additive formulation, constraining the network to generate physically reliable textures. We then design a Mamba refinement architecture for efficient long-range spatial modeling, which efficiently refines the SGP-generated priors through long-range spatial modeling. Additionally, we introduce the Clutter-Aware Attention Gate (CAG) and Residual Refinement Head (RRH) in the Mamba refinement architecture, which can restore the complex textures and high-frequency scattering details. Experiments on SSDD and HRSID datasets provide systematic quantitative and qualitative evidence for the effectiveness of the proposed framework. These results suggest that incorporating scattering-aware physical priors into state-space refinement can provide a useful methodological direction for physically consistent SAR image synthesis. An interactive GUI is also provided to illustrate the controllable synthesis process. Video: https://youtu.be/V31SkO271Ho. Code and datasets: https://github.com/Pluto-cc/SGPMamba.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Mamba-trident: terrain-guided tri-modal Mamba network for mapping little ice age glaciers
abstract: The Little Ice Age (LIA) maximum glacier extent provides a pre-industrial baseline for quantifying centennial-scale glacier retreat. However, post-LIA surface modification weakens the spectral and textural contrasts between glacial deposits and surrounding terrain, limiting reliable mapping from optical or synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery alone. Existing fusion strategies in glacier mapping typically combine heterogeneous modalities without explicitly modeling their physical relationships. To address this limitation, we formulate LIA glacier mapping as a three-class semantic segmentation task over background terrain, modern glaciers, and deglaciated areas, and propose Mamba-Trident, a tri-stream architecture with terrain-guided two-stage cross-modal fusion. In the first stage, DEM features condition the optical and SAR streams to provide a shared topographic context; in the second stage, the conditioned optical and SAR features exchange information to integrate complementary surface characteristics. Evaluated on a Himalayan dataset containing 5,776 LIA glaciers and 9,271 modern glaciers across 18,676 km2, Mamba-Trident achieves state-of-the-art performance with an mIoU of 67.6 % and an LIA maximum extent IoU of 75.6 %. Cross-regional experiments on the Tanggula Mountains and Eastern Tian Shan further demonstrate generalization, achieving mIoU values of 72.4 % and 71.1 %, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of terrain-guided multi-modal learning for automated LIA glacier mapping across diverse mountain regions.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: SFMNet: Joint semantic and structural modeling via spatial–frequency collaboration for remote sensing scene segmentation
abstract: As the spatial resolution of remote sensing imagery continues to improve, Earth observation scenes exhibit greater diversity in spatial and spectral characteristics, together with increasingly complex surface structures across multiple scales. In such scenarios, global land-cover patterns and local high-frequency details are often strongly coupled, posing significant challenges for accurate scene interpretation and boundary delineation. From a feature representation perspective, spatial-domain features are effective for modeling global context and high-level semantics, whereas frequency-domain representations facilitate the separation of structural components at different scales and enhance fine boundary details, but have limited capability in explicitly capturing semantic relationships. Consequently, most existing semantic segmentation methods operate in a single domain, either spatial or frequency, which restricts their ability to jointly model semantic consistency and diverse spatial structures. To address this issue, we propose a semantic segmentation network termed Spatial–Frequency Collaborative Modeling Network (SFMNet), which jointly learns complementary representations in both spatial and frequency domains. By leveraging spatial-domain semantic priors to guide frequency-domain structural enhancement, SFMNet enables coordinated modeling of land-cover semantics and multi-scale surface structures. In addition, cross-scale interaction between low- and high-frequency components and adaptive multi-level feature fusion are introduced to improve structural consistency across hierarchical feature representations. Extensive experiments on the ISPRS Potsdam, Vaihingen, and LoveDA datasets demonstrate that SFMNet consistently outperforms existing methods in both overall segmentation accuracy and boundary delineation quality. Specifically, SFMNet achieves mean Intersection-over-Union scores of 81.30%, 70.23%, and 55.07%, and Boundary mean Intersection-over-Union scores of 65.42%, 56.76%, and 43.74% on the three datasets, respectively.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: DPNet: A disaster perception network for building damage detection using single-temporal remote sensing imagery
abstract: Rapid detection of damaged buildings is critical for effective emergency response following sudden disasters. Although single-temporal methods enable rapid detection without requiring paired pre-event imagery, they often lack disaster-specific awareness, leading to limited accuracy and weak generalization. To address these critical limitations, we propose a disaster perception network (DPNet) tailored for single-temporal high-resolution remote sensing imagery, enabling more precise detection of damaged buildings in various disaster scenarios. DPNet integrates disaster perception module (DPM) to adaptively fuse disaster semantics with building damage features and employs the dynamic semantic-guided multi-task loss (DSML) to enforce cross-task semantic consistency, effectively reducing both false positives and missed detections. Extensive experiments conducted on a large-scale global dataset, encompassing 24 disaster events and 7 distinct disaster types, indicate that DPNet outperforms existing state-of-the-art models by over 7 % in mean intersection over union. Moreover, it significantly surpasses all comparative models on 7 additional unseen disaster events, further validating its generalization capability. These results demonstrate that DPNet enables robust building damage detection, providing a highly reliable and efficient technical solution for global disaster emergency response.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: DNFNet: a brightness-adaptive lightweight RGB–thermal network for day–night UAV wildfire segmentation
abstract: Wildfires significantly threaten human safety and property, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become a crucial tool for regional fire monitoring. To reduce false positives and negatives caused by diurnal lighting changes and modality differences in day–night RGB–Thermal (RGB–T) UAV fire segmentation, we propose DNFNet, a brightness-adaptive, lightweight dual-branch, multi-level complementary fusion network. The method introduces a smooth sigmoid-gated brightness factor to explicitly adjust the fusion weights between RGB and thermal streams. At shallow levels, the Local Detail Enhance-Cross Modal Fusion (LDECMF) Module compensates for the spatial detail deficiency of thermal images; at deeper layers, the Global Semantic Enhance Cross-Modal Fusion (GSECMF) module, along with a Multi-Scale Feature Fusion (MSFF) module, enhances semantic consistency and cross-scale responsiveness. This design allows the collaborative optimization of local boundary accuracy and global semantic coherence. To validate our approach, we constructed DNFire, a UAV RGB–T fire dataset covering diverse scenes, viewpoints, and day-night conditions, and conducted comparative and ablation tests on DNFire and two public datasets against several state-of-the-art methods. Results show that DNFNet achieves an IoU of 0.854 and an F1 score of 0.921 on day–night data, while remaining computationally efficient (12.06 million parameters and 9.15 GFLOPs). The model runs at approximately 25 FPS on low-power edge devices, balancing high accuracy with real-time deployment potential. These results indicate that DNFNet offers a practical, efficient solution for day–night RGB–T UAV wildfire monitoring.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: FGPMamba: Frequency-geometry prior-guided Mamba for building change detection
abstract: Building change detection (BCD) from high-resolution optical remote sensing imagery supports urban monitoring, land-use mapping, and construction progress assessment. However, in arid emerging-city environments, bare land, construction surfaces, concrete roofs, roads, and shadows may resemble changed buildings, resulting in pseudo changes, incomplete regions, and uncertain boundaries. This study proposes a frequency-geometry prior-guided Mamba network (FGPMamba) that combines global context modeling, phase-preserving frequency-domain feature recalibration, gradient-guided global–local fusion, and absolute-difference-based gradient refinement to exploit structural and boundary cues under appearance ambiguity. We also construct the African Desert Emerging-City Building Change Detection dataset (ADEC-CD) using 2018 and 2024 SuperView-2 imagery of Egypt’s New Administrative Capital. ADEC-CD adopts a geographically independent multi-zone split to reduce spatial leakage. On its geographically held-out test set, FGPMamba achieves mean F1, IoU1, Kappa, B-F1, and B-IoU scores of 87.49%, 77.76%, 86.70%, 64.78%, and 40.25%, respectively, over three independent runs. Under dataset-specific training and evaluation, FGPMamba also achieves the highest F1, B-F1, and B-IoU scores among the compared methods on SYSU-CD and HRCUS-CD. Controlled comparisons and feature-response analyses show that the proposed design improves pseudo-change suppression, changed-region completeness, and boundary reliability through frequency-dependent recalibration and boundary-concentrated refinement. These results indicate the potential of FGPMamba for construction monitoring in the study area and potentially similar arid environments. The code and dataset will be publicly available at: https://github.com/zjd1836/FGPMamba.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: GeoSeg-SAM: Task-aligned adaptation of SAM for geological remote sensing interpretation
abstract: The Segment Anything Model (SAM) has shown strong performance in natural image segmentation. However, its direct transfer to geological environment remote sensing (GERS) is limited by significant domain discrepancies. GERS elements typically exhibit high class diversity, strong inter-class similarity, and imbalanced sample distribution, which challenge SAM’s prompt-driven paradigm in maintaining semantic stability and spatial contextual consistency. To bridge this gap, we propose GeoSeg-SAM, a geological task-aligned adaptation framework built upon SAM. GeoSeg-SAM progressively aligns generic visual features with geology-discriminative semantics through layer-wise semantic adapters, and introduces a dual-scale structure-aware module in the deeper encoder layers to enhance global region-level contextual representation. Meanwhile, the model employs Pyramid Residual Aggregation (PRA) to fuse multi-level geological semantic representations across stages, thereby improving the representational capacity of features. In addition, at the mask prediction stage, decoded features are fused with PRA-based semantic representations using a semantics-constrained fusion decoding strategy, and a single geological semantic token is incorporated to enhance semantic consistency in GERS scenarios. Experimental results on three representative GERS study areas show that GeoSeg-SAM improves mIoU by approximately 3 percentage points or more over the best competing method in each area, confirming its effectiveness in GERS image interpretation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/WanZhan-lucky/GeoSeg-SAM.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: MMC-Net: Mamba-based multi-level class-aware network for panchromatic and multispectral fusion classification
abstract: Recent advances in remote sensing (RS) have improved panchromatic (PAN) and multispectral (MS) data acquisition, but challenges remain in multi-source fusion classification due to limitations in non-redundant feature extraction (i.e., effectively preserving complementary information while suppressing source-specific redundancies) and cross-source alignment (i.e., accurately matching spatial–spectral correspondences between PAN and MS data). The emerging state space model (SSM)-based Mamba model, with its global modeling and linear complexity, shows potential for complex land cover classification tasks. To this end, we propose MMC-Net, a novel Mamba-based multi-level class-aware network for PAN and MS fusion classification, which integrates a progressive fusion feature learning (PFFL) module and a multi-branch class-aware classification (MBCAC) module. The PFFL module employs dual-path spatial–spectral Mamba (S2Mamba) to extract discriminative features while suppressing redundancy through the feature reconstruction module (FRM), along with fusion Mamba (FMamba) to enable cross-source interaction via channel exchange and Fusion SSM. The MBCAC module enhances classification diversity through spatial-wise softmax and multi-branch learning, while its parameter-sharing mechanism across levels captures hierarchical discriminative patterns. Validated on three PAN-MS and one HSI-LiDAR datasets, MMC-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance and demonstrates robust, source-agnostic generalization across heterogeneous modalities. The code is available at https://github.com/Xidian-AIGroup190726/MMCNet.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Four decades of vegetation phenology across Europe using PKU GIMMS NDVI: assessing timing, stability and spatial patterns
abstract: Large-scale, long-term analyses of vegetation dynamics provide essential insights into ecosystem functioning and reveal early evidence of environmental change. This study investigates phenological variability and monthly trends across Europe from 1982 to 2022 using the high-accuracy PKU GIMMS NDVI dataset, which offers improved temporal consistency and calibration. We present a novel framework integrating established analytical methods with a newly developed Phenology Variability Index (PVI), designed to assess phenological stability at climatic scales. The framework combines spatially explicit pixel-level analyses, including interdecadal NDVI statistics and PVI evaluations, with clustering methods to identify phenologically homogeneous regions, quantify their variability, and enable inter-cluster comparisons. Following preprocessing and quality control, monthly NDVI series were analysed using non-parametric statistical tests, K-means clustering, Land Surface Phenology (LSP) metrics, and monthly trend estimation. Five spatially coherent clusters were identified, displaying distinct seasonal signatures across ecological zones. Results reveal spatially heterogeneous trends, including consistent greening in temperate, montane, and Mediterranean regions, weaker seasonal greening in semi-arid areas, and largely stable winter NDVI in mountainous forests and continental areas. LSP metrics indicate shifts in the timing and duration of growing seasons, consistent with climate- and land use- driven phenological change. The PVI further highlights higher phenological stability in Mediterranean landscapes and semi-arid regions and greater variability in montane forests and temperate zones. This integrated approach enhances understanding of vegetation responses to environmental variability across scales and provides a robust methodological basis for long-term ecosystem monitoring, supporting both applied geoinformation analyses and broader ecological research.
journal_title: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: Differential land deformation patterns and response mechanism to groundwater recovery in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei Plain revealed by reconstructing and clustering of TS-InSAR observations
abstract: The Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei (BTH) Plain in north China has experienced significant land subsidence due to long-term groundwater overexploitation. Although water diversion project and climate change have improved groundwater conditions overall, the spatiotemporal heterogeneity in land deformation responses to groundwater recovery remains unclear. This study reconstructs and identifies differentiated deformation patterns across the BTH Plain under the new hydrological background, revealing their multi-scale response mechanisms to groundwater change. After mosaicking Time-Series Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (TS-InSAR) deformation fields, we reconstructed the seasonal and long-term components of deformation. A long-term deformation characteristic-constrained K-means clustering method was developed to classify distinct deformation evolution patterns. Coupling these patterns with groundwater-level (GWL) observations to further distinguish the annual lag and long-term delayed response of deformation to GWL changes. From 2016 to 2024, the BTH Plain exhibits clear spatial partitioning of deformation behaviors, categorized as 10.14% continuous subsidence, 18.86% reduced subsidence, 46.09% stable deformation, and 24.91% slight rebound. Uncertainties in the reconstructed deformation reflect short-term fluctuations driven by extreme hydrological or anthropogenic disturbances. Short-time Fourier transform analysis reveals periodic response of deformation to GWL change and annual lag: elastic deformation dominated areas lag GWL by ≤ 2 months, whereas clay-rich persistent subsiding areas lag 4–6 months. The exponential decay model further indicates that the recovery of subsidence funnels is governed by geological structures: funnels intersecting faults show the slowest subsidence decay along their edges, while those without faults display a more uniform edge-to-center recovery pattern.

title: An adaptive hybrid algorithm for retrieving particulate organic carbon in complex coastal waters
abstract: The retrieval of particulate organic carbon (POC) from optical properties in coastal waters remains a significant challenge because of profound spatiotemporal heterogeneity in water composition. Here, we propose an adaptive hybrid algorithm for POC retrieval (AHA-POC). This algorithm integrates optical water cluster classification with cluster specific model optimization to deliver improved POC estimates in optically complex environments, as demonstrated for the coastal waters of Guangdong and eastern Hainan Island. The algorithm first defines bio-optical water clusters using K-means clustering based on inherent optical properties (IOPs) and derived composite features. This classification separated samples into optically distinct clusters characterized by systematic differences in particle composition, absorption and scattering properties, and bio-optical relationships, which reduce the influence of variability in aquatic particulate matter composition on subsequent POC retrieval algorithms. After cluster definition, cluster specific sensitive features and retrieval models were selected to account for variable POC–IOPs relationships across optical regimes. To avoid station level data leakage, model performance was evaluated using leave-one-station-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV), in which all samples from the same station were held out together during validation. The AHA-POC achieved stable retrieval performance (R2 = 0.79, RMSE = 0.071 mg /L, MAPE = 32.38 %, Bias = -0.78 %), showing improved accuracy relative to both univariate retrieval models and threshold-based water classification schemes in optically complex water environments. The algorithm was further applied to high resolution in situ IOPs profiles to reconstruct POC sections at 1 m vertical resolution, revealing fine scale vertical heterogeneity associated with riverine plume influence and near bottom particle resuspension. These results demonstrate the potential of cluster specific optical modeling for improving regional POC estimation in optically complex coastal waters and for supporting high resolution assessments of coastal carbon variability.

title: Large-scale building instance segmentation in diverse urban scenes based on LiDAR data
abstract: Building 3D profiles constitute critical factors in urban environmental analyses, including assessments of urban heat island effects, carbon emissions, population distribution, and related challenges. LiDAR data provide comprehensive high-resolution 3D information, enabling the acquisition of detailed 3D building profiles. However, in dense urban environments, buildings are in diverse shapes and heights, and are close to one another, making it challenging to extract building instances. In this paper, we propose BuildGroup, a novel building instance segmentation model for both Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS)-based and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) datasets. It employs the progressive learning strategy in the feature aggregation, which uses prior 2D knowledge from the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to infer spatial relationships within point clouds and mitigate cross-source discrepancies. An offset enhancement module is introduced to mitigate the effects of diverse point densities, improving instance clustering by compacting point cloud distributions. Additionally, an edge-enhanced loss function prioritizes boundary point accuracy during training to enhance morphological precision. Furthermore, we present a building LiDAR dataset with instance-level building information, which fills a key gap in real-world, large-scale urban point cloud segmentation, particularly for ALS-based sparse façade data. Experimental results validate the framework’s capability to produce accurate building instance information across varying urban densities. All code and data are available at https://github.com/littlebeen/BuildGroup.
